content: A preventorium was a specialized institution or facility established for individuals infected with tuberculosis who had not yet developed the active form of the disease. These facilities gained popularity in the early 20th century and were specifically designed to isolate such patients from both uninfected individuals and those exhibiting overt symptoms of tuberculosis. The primary goal was to prevent the progression of the disease and to minimize the risk of transmission. The first preventorium was founded in 1909 by philanthropist Nathan Straus in Lakewood, New Jersey. This initiative marked a significant step in public health efforts to combat tuberculosis during that era.
